terms.grammar: ferō with the adverb aegrē; the thing as object, or the accusative and infinitive
evidence: Cic. Tusc. 4.17.40: aegrē ferre repulsam cōnsulātūs (Lewis & Short), s.v. ferō
terms.comment: Also molestē ferre and, more strongly, graviter ferre.
Traupman’s phrase; not in Lewis & Short or the loci collections.

sources: Lewis & Short: aegre · Lewis & Short: fero
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 100, checked against the searchable text and the page image (12 November 2026).
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
